newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech SPT Telecom sinks in bear market.
newsitem.headline: Czech SPT Telecom sinks in bear market.

text.p: Shares in SPT Telecom, the most heavily capitalised issue on the Prague bourse, plunged on Wednesday with dealers blaming a general decline in confidence in the Czech equity market rather than company fundamentals.
SPT lost 124 crowns, 4.1 percent, to 2,866 after the first 30 minutes of continuous trading on the bourse, putting it 14 percent below its price at the beginning of October.
"The whole market has no support whatsoever. There are no fundamental changes to SPT," said Jan Sykora of Wood & Company in Prague.
Sykora said the market "could easily go down another five or 10 or 15 percent," and suggested that SPT could follow the market down.

Czech equities have been sharply hit in recent weeks with investors more and more openly saying they are reluctant to invest on the Prague Stock Exchange until an adequate framework for transparency and the protection of minority shareholders is put in place.
Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus long riduculed the need for such regulations but the government says it is now addressing the matter.
